name: Delhivery Ltd
title: Delhivery Ltd - 543529 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Delhivery Q1 FY27: revenue ~Rs3,000 Cr (+28% YoY) with PTL yield up to ~Rs12/kg and FY27 guidance narrowed to 20-30% growth, but profitability hit by two new contracts and labour costs; supply-side signals are light.

triggers.label: PTL yield up ~20% YoY
triggers.quote: yield continued to improve in the PTL

evasions.quote: the coverage is not 100%, I can confirm almost, almost 100%

summary.headline: Delhivery Q1 FY27 revenue rose 28% YoY to nearly Rs.3,000 Cr, with PAT of Rs.17 Cr after a Rs.15 Cr-plus cost drag from two new contracts and unused assets.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 as a record quarter for revenue but a weak one for profitability, hit by chronic labour shortages, election and weather disruptions, and start-up costs for two large new contracts. Express acquisition consolidation drove much of the 55% YoY growth in the reported figures. PTL yield rose to nearly Rs.12 per kg (per management's wording), and management attributed most of the improvement to organic gains rather than pass-through. Diesel price hikes in May are being passed through to customers with a lag, and management said FY27 outlook is unchanged at 20-30% growth.

financial_highlights.value: Rs.17 Cr (stat P&L ~Rs.30 Cr before ROU/intangible-related items)
financial_highlights.change: Management said PAT before unused-asset costs was ~Rs.62 Cr in press release; reconciliation given on call
Target 16-18% long term; internal exit target 15-15.5%
Stable across FY25, FY26 and Q1 FY27

financial_highlights.value: ~Rs.35 Cr per management, Rs.30-35 Cr normalised
financial_highlights.change: Relates to Rs.17 Cr in Q1 and delay in Q2
Q1 average linehaul cost ~12.2% of revenue, up ~0.6 pp (diesel)

segments.name: Express / e-commerce & B2B
segments.commentary: Express EBITDA margin exited at 13.4%, with an internal target of 15-15.5% exit and 16-18% long-term. Q1 growth of 55% was flattered by Express base effects, since the acquisition was reported in full only from Q2.

segments.name: PTL (Part Truck Load)
segments.commentary: Tonnage of 542,000 tonnes (+18% YoY) and yield of nearly Rs.12/kg (+20% YoY). Management said most of the yield gain was organic, about 37 paise per kg improvement, of which 6 paise was fuel-linked pass-through.

segments.name: Supply Chain Services (SCS)
segments.commentary: Two new large contracts (industrials and durables) depressed margins in Q1 during fulfilment-centre build-up; billing starts on outbound, so inbound buildup costs are front-loaded. Management expects stabilisation over Q2 and early Q3.

segments.name: New initiatives (Local, Direct, Maps)
segments.commentary: Local ARR is at Rs.150 Cr in July, versus an earlier target of Rs.250 Cr exit ARR for FY27; management revised its expectation to Rs.160-175 Cr. Ahmedabad Local is expected to break even around month three. NBFC approval received in July.

guidance_outlook: Management maintained the FY27 revenue growth guidance of 20-30%; the range is wider because the outcome depends on Q2 and early Q3 trends.
FY27 profitability and medium/long-term targets were said to be unchanged, with no major structural headwinds seen by management.
Diesel: management says the pass-through is almost 100% covered (97-98% per Varun Bakshi). July is expected to reflect the May diesel hike with the lag gone.
Corporate manpower costs estimated at Rs.371 Cr for FY27 (as stated on call).
Unused-asset (lock-in/ROU) costs of around Rs.17 Cr are expected to continue until disposal, per management, and are treated as ongoing rather than one-time.
capex_capacity: Two new large SCS contracts required build-up of multiple fulfilment sites with a 45-60 day lead to inbound stock before outbound billing ramps.
Automation: in-facility movement and automated storage/retrieval being introduced at key transportation and fulfilment facilities.
Maps (proprietary GIS) launched on 8 August for internal deployment, with external availability planned later.
Expansion of cross-sell development teams for truck and LCV businesses; coverage now 100% of India versus earlier top-3 cities.
demand_pricing: Demand continued into Q2, with festive-season sales starting to lift volumes; August to date is said to be robust.
D2C volumes are running at 40-45% of PTL volumes and skew to heavier packages, which supports yields.
Pricing contracts are indexed to the prevailing month's diesel rate. Diesel-driven revisions were under negotiation from late April to mid-May, and pass-throughs are expected to show in Q2.
Management said pricing pressure has eased, with no price cuts for customers and reduced irrational competition. Competitor price cuts were disputed by management as not matching its own contracts.
New customer adds were mainly D2C and SME; management said self-serve sign-up through DelhiveryOne is growing.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the 20-30% revenue growth guidance range, and what is the trend in new customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 was soft seasonally but robust after adjusting for Express, and the range is wider because Q2 and early Q3 trends are still forming. New customers are mostly D2C and SME, with festive demand building.

qa_highlights.question: Is the PTL yield increase seasonal or sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yield gains are planned and organic, with about 37 paise per kg of improvement, of which 6 paise was fuel pass-through; the sustained QoQ improvement is expected to continue.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the 300 bps margin pressure is from diesel versus other costs, and how quickly can it be passed on?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fuel is about 0.6 pp of revenue for PTL; the bigger hit is labour-related minimum wage and rider payout linkage, which lacks a pass-through clause. Diesel revisions have been mostly passed through, and the effect should be evident in Q2.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the NBFC (asset-light lending) plan matter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not lend heavily from its own balance sheet, but will partner with lending firms and underwrite a part of exposure to help fleet owners get insurance and financing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the PAT difference between the press release and reported figures (Rs.62 Cr vs Rs.32 Cr vs Rs.17 Cr)?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Rs.17 Cr relates to unused lock-in assets and facilities; the stat P&L shows about Rs.30 Cr after ROU and depreciation items. Shah queried recurrence, and management said the unused-asset costs are recurring until disposal.

qa_highlights.question: Why did SCS margins decline and what is the new-contract economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said two new large contracts started together and are in an inbound-heavy build-up phase with negative cash flows, but they are expected to stabilise in Q2 and early Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Is Delhivery exposed to competition from in-house or 3PL consolidation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has gained share, with volumes retained through the uncertain environment, and that in-house consolidation is an encouraging but unproven trend.
